text_blocks.snippet: Preventing roof ice dams in Utah—especially in higher-elevation and mountain-valley areas like Heber City where heavy snowpack and freeze-thaw cycles are common—requires [Highlight start] keeping your attic cold and managing snow along the eaves [Highlight end] .
snippet_highlighted_words: [Highlight start] keeping your attic cold and managing snow along the eaves [Highlight end]

list.snippet: Seal air leaks: Air leaks from living spaces warm the attic and melt roof snow unevenly. Seal gaps around light fixtures, hatches, plumbing, and wiring.
Insulate and ventilate: Maintain adequate attic insulation and balanced soffit-to-ridge ventilation so the roof deck stays close to outdoor temperatures.

Install ice and water shield: Use self-adhering waterproof underlayment along eaves and valleys during roofing or reroofing (high-temperature ratings are typically required under metal roofing) to block water backup if an ice dam forms .
Rake snow after storms: Use a roof rake from the ground to pull snow off the lower 3–4 feet of the roof edge before melt-refreeze cycles build up.
Clear gutters and downspouts: Clean leaves and debris in fall, and keep downspouts clear during winter so meltwater can drain.
Add heat cables selectively: Roof de-icing cables along eaves and downspouts can help keep drainage paths open in problem spots, though they do not fix underlying attic heat loss.

text_blocks.snippet: If an Ice Dam Already Forms

list.snippet: Avoid chipping ice with hammers, axes, or sharp tools, which can tear shingles or injure you .

For minor localized buildup, homeowners sometimes drape calcium-chloride ice melt inside a nylon stocking across the dam from the roof edge to melt a drainage channel, or hire a contractor using low-pressure steam.

text_blocks.snippet: To narrow this down for your home, share your approximate elevation or city (such as Heber City vs. the Salt Lake valley), roof type (asphalt shingle or metal), and whether you are preventing future dams or dealing with active leaks.
